newsitem.title: GREECE: Angry Greek farmers threaten fresh road blocks.
newsitem.headline: Angry Greek farmers threaten fresh road blocks.

text.p: Greek farmers threatened on Thursday to repeat crippling road blockades that cut the country in two last month if their demands for financial help from the government are not satisfied by February 4.
"We are warning the government 20 days ahead of time in order to avoid bringing tractors out in the streets," farmers' representative Yannis Patakis told Greek television.

A 25-day blockade in December paralysed road traffic and left thousands of trucks stranded along highways. The farmers suspended their action during the Christmas and New year holidays but vowed to repeat it if demands were not met.
Demands include lower fuel costs and Value Added Tax (VAT) on farm equipment, higher price supports, especially for cotton, and a $1.3 billion rescheduling of debts to the state Agricultural Bank.
From January 28, farmers in central Greece will launch a series of protests, mostly disrupting public services, to warn the government they mean business ahead of a full-scale blockade, Patakis said.
"We will block public services, tax offices and toll booths in our area to prevent the state from collecting money," he said.
